label: myadhd.my
caption:
Guitar. Sourdough. Running. Crochet. All in one year.

Diving into a new hobby, then dropping it, is common with ADHD. Swipe for why the spark fades so fast, and three ways to keep the good parts.

If this sounded like your brain, come sit with people who get it. Our group is in my bio 👇

Save this before you buy the next starter kit.

#adhd #adhdmalaysia #myadhd #adhdadult #adhdhobbies

slides.title:
Why do I quit
every new
[[hobby]]?
slides.sub: You are not flaky. New things just light you up.

slides.title:
New things
[[light up]]
your brain
slides.body: A fresh hobby is full of novelty. Every video, every tool, every first try feels exciting. That rush is real fuel for an ADHD brain.

slides.title:
Then the
novelty [[fades]]
slides.body: Week three, it is just practice. Same chords, same mistakes. The spark that carried you is gone, and nothing has replaced it yet.

slides.title:
The kit stays,
the [[guilt]] grows
slides.body: Paints in the cupboard, a guitar in the corner, a gym card in the wallet. Each one feels like proof you never finish anything.

slides.title:
You still
[[learned]]
something
slides.body: Three months of anything is still three months. You picked up skills, met people and had fun. A hobby can end without being a failure.

slides.title:
[[Borrow]]
before you
buy
slides.body: Rent it, borrow it, take one class first. Let the excitement settle before the money goes in.

slides.title:
Rotate instead
of [[quitting]]
slides.body: Keep two or three hobbies on a loop. When one goes stale, switch, and come back to it later. It will feel fresh again.

slides.title:
Do it with
[[someone]]
slides.body: A class, a club, a friend who expects you on Saturday. Other people keep a hobby going on the weeks the spark is low.

slides.title:
Save this before
you buy the next
[[starter kit]]
slides.body: Loving new things is part of how your brain works. Dump the ideas into my.adhd and get one thing back to try this week.
